ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT legislation is the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184. Quebec corporate beneficial-ownership disclosure is governed principally by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1, and the Regulation respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1, r. 1. Federal corporations are governed by the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, including beneficial-ownership record requirements. Quebec's enterprise register is maintained by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. Securities registration, prospectus, dealer, adviser, and investment-fund-manager requirements are governed principally by the Securities Act (Quebec), CQLR, c. V-1.1, related regulations, and applicable Canadian Securities Administrators instruments. A venture-capital general partner or management company must separately assess whether it is an investment fund manager, portfolio manager, exempt market dealer, adviser, or another regulated registrant.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access with significant public disclosure for Quebec entities: Quebec enterprise-register information concerning individuals who control or own a reporting enterprise may be publicly searchable, subject to statutory exclusions, masking, safety restrictions, and implementation limitations. Financial institutions, securities registrants, and other reporting entities must maintain and verify beneficial-ownership information under federal AML legislation. Nominee arrangements do not eliminate disclosure, verification, recordkeeping, or sanctions obligations.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct risk-based screening before incorporation, banking, capital acceptance, and each material transaction. Screen all beneficial owners, directors, officers, authorized signatories, fund principals, investors where required, counterparties, and relevant family members or close associates against United Nations Security Council sanctions, Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act and Special Economic Measures Act, Canadian Criminal Code terrorist listings, FINTRAC and Canadian regulatory guidance, OFAC lists where a U.S. nexus exists, and applicable domestic or transaction-specific lists. Obtain PEP, head-of-international-organization, family-member, and close-associate declarations; document source of wealth and source of funds; apply enhanced due diligence, senior approval, transaction monitoring, and suspicious transaction reporting where required. Do not treat a negative database result as conclusive evidence of identity or legitimacy.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services portal, including the enterprise-name search and registration services; for federal incorporation, Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre and the Nuans corporate-name search system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Quebec corporation must comply with the Charter of the French Language and applicable enterprise-name rules. The French name must be acceptable for use in Quebec, and the name must not be confusing with an existing name, misleading, contrary to public order, or improperly descriptive of a regulated activity. An English or other-language version may be used only subject to Quebec language-law requirements and applicable registration rules. A federal corporation must satisfy the Canada Business Corporations Act name rules and obtain a Nuans search where required. Transliteration does not cure confusion, descriptiveness, language, trademark, or regulated-word objections. Corporate-name clearance is not trademark clearance.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying a financial, securities, insurance, public authority, educational, charitable, or regulated professional status without the required approval or licence
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Confirm whether the filing is for a Quebec entity or a federal corporation because the reservation and clearance mechanisms differ. Obtain a current Quebec enterprise-name search and, for a federal corporation, a Nuans report where applicable. File the proposed name, French-language analysis, corporate purpose, and supporting approvals through the applicable registry portal. If rejected, obtain the written reason, preserve the filing reference, and determine whether the issue is confusion, language, descriptiveness, prohibited wording, trademark risk, or regulated-activity implication. Submit a revised name or written request for reconsideration with evidence of consent, distinctiveness, regulatory approval, or non-confusion. Where a statutory administrative appeal or review is available, file within the deadline stated in the decision and retain proof of service. A court application for judicial review may be available for a reviewable administrative decision; legal counsel should confirm the applicable limitation period. Do not commence operations under a rejected or unregistered name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A corporation must maintain a registered office address in the applicable jurisdiction and must be able to receive official service and maintain required records. A conventional virtual-office arrangement may be acceptable for registry purposes if it provides a genuine address, reliable document receipt, and access to corporate records, but a post-office box alone is insufficient. For a venture-capital general partner or management entity, a bare virtual office is high risk for bank onboarding, securities registration, source-of-funds review, tax residency, transfer-pricing support, and institutional-investor diligence. The entity should maintain documented management functions, decision-making records, books and records, authorized personnel, compliance controls, and premises proportionate to its activity. Registration, licensing, and fund-administration requirements may impose additional location and record-access conditions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official Canadian or Quebec statistical probability is published. Internal planning estimate: approximately 5-15 percent annual likelihood for an ordinary low-risk registered-office verification event, increasing to approximately 15-35 percent during securities registration, financial-institution onboarding, AML escalation, tax audit, complaint investigation, unusual cross-border activity, or high-risk ownership review. These are non-statutory risk estimates, not government statistics. Unannounced inspections or site visits are more likely where the entity presents as a regulated financial business, has inconsistent substance, uses a nominee structure, or cannot demonstrate operational control.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Québec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 3, 10, 16, 41, 44, 49, 51, 52, 113, 116, 128; Act respecting the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, CQLR c R-13.1, ss. 5, 26
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Corporate Constitution Service and Enterprise Register
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) filed electronically with the REQ; Certificate of Constitution issued upon registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required under the QBCA; shares may be issued for any consideration fixed by the board of directors; no statutory escrow account or capital deposit is required for a general-purpose venture capital GP holding corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation accepts the subscriptions of the Incorporators for its authorized share capital in the amounts recorded in the Share Subscription Register, full payment of which has been received in cash. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is established at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and the Board authorizes the Secretary to file any required notice of change with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. RESOLVED, that the following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each holding office at the pleasure of the Board. RESOLVED, that the General By-law No. 1 is adopted and the President is authorized to issue share certificates to the subscribers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation via NUANS Search and REQ Reservation Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Name Reservation Window; Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) NUANS system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search through an authorized private search house or the REQ online portal to confirm the proposed bilingual corporate name is distinctive and not confusing. Submit an online Name Reservation Application to the REQ via the Espace clients portal, specifying the proposed english and french forms, the activities (NAICS 525910 / ISIC 6499), and the consent of any named individuals. Pay the CAD reservation fee electronically. If approved, the REQ issues a Name Reservation Certificate valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS name search report (dated within 90 days)
Name reservation application form with two alternative names
Declaration of intended primary business activities
Identification of the incorporation applicant and incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ rejects the name for confusion or non-distinctiveness, submit a revised application within the same fee term or file an attestation of distinctiveness supported by trade-mark registration evidence. If the reservation lapses, re-apply with a renewed NUANS report before filing articles of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Articles of Incorporation and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Corporate Constitution Centre (Centre de constitution des personnes morales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the REQ online system and complete the 'Constitution of a Business Corporation' form. Provide the reserved name, registered office address in Quebec, share structure (class, rights, number), name and municipality of each director, and the name of the sole incorporator. Declare any restrictions on the business or the transfer of shares if desired. Electronically sign the statutory declaration and pay the CAD 370 constitution fee plus the CAD 32 enterprise registration fee. Upon approval, the REQ issues the Certificate of Constitution and the enterprise number (NEQ). Notarization is not mandatory; the electronic signature of the incorporator suffices.
required_dossiers: Valid Name Reservation Certificate
Articles of Incorporation draft (form S-11 equivalent)
Director consent and declaration (name, address, email)
Registered office address within Quebec
Authorized share capital structure and restrictions
Proof of payment of constitution and registration fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of refusal or a request for further information, respond in writing within 30 days, amend the articles online, and re-submit. If the decision is adverse, file a formal review application with the REQ under CQLR c R-13.1 within the statutory delay, or re-constitute under a corrected corporate name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Registration, NEQ Activation and Public Registry Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises (Enterprise Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the certificate of constitution, verify that the enterprise registration is automatically activated in the REQ database. Confirm the registrant club membership (NEQ number) and complete the mandatory initial declaration, specifying the establishment address, the primary activity ISIC/NAICS code (ISIC 6499 / NAICS 525910), the date of commencement of activities, and the list of directors and officers. Maintain the registered office address as the default address for service in the register.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Constitution
Enterprise initial registration declaration (Déclaration d'immatriculation)
List of directors and officers with residential addresses
Registered office and establishment addresses
NEQ activation request and fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the automatic registration is delayed or incomplete, file a written amendment via Form D-1 at REQ or through the online portal. Correct any discrepancies in the registry by filing a declaration of change within 15 days; if the NEQ cannot be activated, re-submit the initial declaration with certified proof of incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of By-Law No. 1, Officer Appointments and Issuance of Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation; corporate minute book maintained at the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the initial directors or procure written consent of all directors in lieu of the meeting. Adopt the General By-law No. 1 governing meetings, quorum, voting, officers, indemnification, and banking. Fix the number of officers, appoint the President, Secretary and Treasurer, and authorize bank account opening. Approve the issuance of common shares to the general partner entity or holding persons, and execute and deliver the corresponding share certificates. Record all resolutions in the corporate minute book and securities register.
required_dossiers: First directors' written resolution or minutes
General By-law No. 1 text approved
Share subscription list and consideration records
Authors for share certificates (paper certificates)
Minute book, securities register, and share transfer ledger
Oath of office or declarations of officers, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum is defective or the by-law adoption is otherwise invalid, execute a written waiver of notice for all directors and re-circulate the resolution. If share certificates are rejected due to technical errors, cancel and re-issue them under a fresh board resolution without additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Account Registration (GST/HST and QST), Payroll Enrollment and AMF Regulatory Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec - Registration Services; Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) - Registration Division (Bureau de l'inscription)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a CRA Business Number (BN) and GST/HST account under section 240 of the Excise Tax Act using Business Registration Online; register separately with Revenu Québec for the QST using Form RD-1. If hiring employees, enroll a payroll program with CRA and Revenu Québec (source deductions and CNESST occupational health contribution). For regulated VC GP activity, file a pre-registration questionnaire with the AMF and complete Form 31-103F1 for registrant dealing in exempt market securities, including corporate history, dual-capability declaration, and AML/ATF program adoption. Keep all registrations updated with any change in directors or capital structure.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Constitution and NEQ number
Registered office and establishment addresses
Identification of shareholders, directors and officers
AML/ATF policies and procedures manual (Canada PCMLTFA and Quebec AML regime)
Criminal record declarations for directors and officers
Proof of liability insurance and proficiency, as required by AMF
Business plan and fund documentation for EMD/IFM review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec rejects the account application, provide corrected identification documents and re-file using the BN. If the AMF issues a 60-day request for additional information, respond with the required exhibits; if registration is refused, file a demarche de révision under the Securities Act and, in the alternative, adjust the corporate activities to avoid the exempt market dealer registration trigger or rely on available registration exemptions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) - Registration Division (Bureau de l'inscription) for securities-related authorization; Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) for the public enterprise registration certificate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Exempt Market Dealer (EMD) and Investment Fund Manager (IFM) registration certificate under the Securities Act (Québec), CQLR c V-1.1; combined with the REQ Certificate of Registration (NEQ) for the enterprise

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Direction de l'évaluation environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Tier III - Registration (Déclaration) category under the Regulation respecting the application of the Environment Quality Act for low-impact office occupancy; no full EIA report required for standard professional offices; exemption may apply where no contaminant-emitting equipment is installed
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluent discharge; sanitary wastewater shall meet municipal sewer by-laws (Montreal standard: pH 5.5-9.5, BOD5 ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L); volatile organic compounds limited to trace emissions from office cleaning products (≤ 100 g VOC per container per incidence); electronic waste and fluorescent lamps must be disposed through MELCCFP-certified recyclers under the Residual Materials Management Policy; office noise emissions ≤ 45 dB at the property line during daytime hours

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety occupancy certificate issued by the municipal fire prevention service in compliance with the Building Act (CQLR c B-1.1) and the Québec Safety Code (R.R.Q., c. B-1.1, r. 10); annual fire alarm and extinguisher inspection certificates; structural load clearance certificate issued by a licensed structural engineer where lease loads exceed 3.0 kPa; workplace hazard prevention program and occupational health clearance pursuant to the Act respecting Occupational Health and Safety (CQLR c S-2.1), including CNESST attestation of the prevention program and employee training records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada) — federal tax authority for corporate income tax, GST/HST and payroll; online portals: CRA 'Business Registration Online' (BRO) and CRA 'My Business Account'. In Quebec: Revenu Quebec (Agence du revenu du Quebec) — provincial tax authority for QST, Quebec corporate income tax under the Taxation Act, Quebec pension plan (QPIP) and employer payroll; online portal: Revenu Quebec 'Business Account' (mon dossier d'entreprise / ClicSUR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Determine whether the foreign VC GP 'carries on business' in Canada (permanent establishment under ITA s. 253 and GST/HST nexus under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act) or makes taxable supplies in Canada. 2. Register online via CRA 'Business Registration Online' (BRO) or by filing Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' to obtain the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN), which functions as the TIN. 3. Simultaneously open a GST/HST account on the same application, obtaining the GST/HST program account (BN + 'RT' suffix + 4-digit reference number). 4. In Quebec, register with Revenu Quebec using the harmonized registration application (Form LM-1 / online 'Registre des entreprises' one-stop), which opens the QST account (BN + 'TQ' suffix), the Quebec corporate income tax account, the QPIP and employer health fund accounts, and the CNESST worker-compensation account where applicable. 5. Foreign (non-resident) registrants must provide a registered representative or attorney in Canada/Quebec, and CRA may require security (ETA s. 307) for GST/HST liabilities. 6. A non-Quebec resident corporation carrying on business in Quebec must also extra-provincially register with the Quebec Enterprise Registrar (Registraire des entreprises) and file a power of attorney with Revenu Quebec. 7. All registrations and amendments are made online at zero statutory fee; the BN and program suffixes serve as the single tax identifier for all CRA and Revenu Quebec filings. 8. Where the GP acts as an investment fund manager or exempt market dealer, separate licensing with the Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) is required but is independent of, and does not replace, tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A business corporation incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act or a Quebec provincial companies statute is a separate taxable 'person' under the Income Tax Act (Part I), the Excise Tax Act (Part IX, GST/HST), the Quebec Taxation Act and the QST Act. It is taxed at the corporate level on worldwide income if resident in Canada (or on Canadian-source income if non-resident), files its own corporate income tax returns (T2 and Quebec CO-17), and is a distinct GST/HST and QST registrant. It is not a pass-through entity. The VC fund is typically a limited partnership (income-tax flow-through) or trust, but the GP corporation is taxed at entity level; carried interest allocated to the GP corporation is corporate income, and management fees charged by the GP to the fund are taxable supplies for GST/HST and QST purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a U.S.-style 'check-the-box' regime; every corporation is per se a separate taxpayer. Statutory elections available to the GP structure include: (1) ITA s. 216 election — a non-resident corporation may elect to file a Canadian return and be taxed on a net basis on Canadian rental/royalty income (limited relevance to a VC GP); (2) ITA s. 250(2) election — a foreign corporation may elect to be deemed resident in Canada; (3) ETA s. 273 election — closely related corporations may elect to treat taxable supplies made between them as being for nil consideration (GST/HST simplification), mirrored for QST by QST Act s. 264; (4) ETA s. 156 joint venture election — co-venturers may elect one 'operator' to account for GST/HST on a joint venture; (5) Hybrid mismatch rules under Part XII.7 of the ITA apply by statutory default rather than by election, with exclusions and ordering rules that may be documented/electively applied to prevent adjustment where 'dual inclusion income' exists; (6) Quebec: parallel elections under the QST Act and the Taxation Act (Quebec), including nil-consideration elections for closely related persons and the Quebec equivalent of the s. 216 election. Pass-through tax treatment for the fund itself is achieved only by structuring as a limited partnership or trust; no election can convert the GP corporation into a flow-through entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added taxation levied as the federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15), plus the Quebec Sales Tax (QST / TVQ) under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax (CQLR c. T-0.1). Quebec does not participate in the Harmonized Sales Tax; the GST (5%) and QST (9.975%) are assessed on the same pre-tax consideration (QST is computed on the price before GST), producing a combined headline rate of 14.975%. Management fees charged by the GP to the venture fund are taxable supplies subject to GST/QST unless zero-rated or exempt; carried interest allocations, being profit shares of a partnership, are not consideration for a supply and remain outside the GST/HST and QST systems.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 — the 'small supplier' threshold under ETA s. 240(1): mandatory registration applies to any person (including a non-resident) making or intending to make taxable supplies in Canada unless total worldwide taxable supplies in the last four consecutive calendar quarters plus the current quarter are C$30,000 or less (special attribution rules apply to non-resident suppliers of intangibles and digital services). The QST registration threshold under the QST Act is aligned at C$30,000. A VC GP earning management fees above C$30,000 on a rolling four-quarter basis is required to register for GST/HST and QST; a non-resident carrying on business in Canada is also required to obtain a corporate income tax account irrespective of the small supplier threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based pre-authorization of invoices exists at the federal or Quebec level. Invoices must satisfy documentary evidence rules (ETA s. 169/286 and QST Act s. 482) but may be issued on paper, PDF, EDI (EDIFACT) or XML. Canada has adopted the Pan-Canadian e-Invoice standard based on the European PEPPOL framework on a voluntary basis; Revenu Quebec accepts PEPPOL and interoperable e-invoicing formats. Mandatory electronic filing: GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via CRA 'My Business Account' / GST/HST NETFILE where annual gross revenue exceeds C$1 million; QST returns must be filed electronically through Revenu Quebec's e-service portal where QST turnover exceeds C$1 million. Electronic payment of GST/HST and QST is mandatory for all registrants. No invoice-level government clearance or cryptographic stamping is imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: (1) Goods: A supply of goods is zero-rated for GST/HST under Schedule VI, Part V of the ETA where the supplier exports the goods, delivers them to a common carrier for export, or the non-resident purchaser exports them within 60 days as part of the supply (ETA Sch. VI Pt. V ss. 1-8); the QST Act contains mirror zero-rating provisions (QST Act s. 194 et seq.). The exporter must retain proof of physical export. (2) Services: Advisory, consulting, management and research services supplied by a GP to a non-resident fund are zero-rated under ETA Sch. VI Pt. V s. 7 where the recipient is a non-resident person not registered for GST/HST, the supply is not in respect of Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada, and the service is acquired for consumption wholly outside Canada; a parallel rule exists under the QST Act. (3) The GP must obtain and retain 'non-resident status' evidence (foreign tax residence certificate, articles of incorporation, certificate of good standing) and documents demonstrating offshore performance and consumption (contracts, engagement letters, invoices, time records, emails, board materials). (4) Input tax credits (GST/HST) and QST input tax refunds may be claimed on inputs attributable to zero-rated exports. (5) Management fees charged to a Canadian-resident fund (including a Canadian-resident limited partnership) remain taxable at the combined 14.975% rate and cannot be zero-rated merely because the fund's investors are non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A — Canada Export Declaration filed with the CBSA, or Canadian Automated Export Declaration (CAED) system filing, for controlled/high-value goods)
Bill of Lading (through/port-to-port) or Airway Bill evidencing delivery outside Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT inbound payment instruction evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Commercial Export Invoice (supplier's invoice showing zero-rating basis)
Packing List / Cargo Manifest (for tangible goods)
Proof of physical export (forwarder's cargo receipt, carrier certificate, terminal receipt, customs stamp)
Executed services agreement and engagement letter with the non-resident fund (for services)
Non-resident status evidence (foreign tax residence certificate or certified copy of constitutional documents)
Bank statements and currency conversion records linking settled export proceeds to the Canadian exporter
CBSA eManifest data or in-transit movement records where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Quebec may reassess a claimed zero-rated export within the 4-year normal reassessment period (ETA s. 298 and parallel QST Act rules), with no limitation period where misrepresentation, neglect or fraud is established. If the exporter fails to substantiate export within the required time (e.g., goods not exported within 60 days or deficient documentation), the zero-rating is clawed back and the GP is assessed for unremitted GST/HST and QST at the combined 14.975% rate on the export consideration, plus daily compounding arrears interest. Civil penalties: ETA s. 285 — false statements/omissions — penalty equal to the greater of C$250 and 25% of the net-tax understatement; ETA s. 285.1 — gross negligence — penalty equal to the greater of C$250 and 50% of the tax sought to be evaded; parallel penalty rules apply under the QST Act. Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable for unremitted GST/HST and QST (ETA s. 323 and the analogous QST Act director-liability provision) where the corporation failed to exercise due diligence. In cases of deliberate fraud, the Criminal Code (s. 380 — fraud against Her Majesty) applies; CRA criminal investigation may lead to prosecution fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and/or imprisonment, in addition to the full retrospective clawback and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential bank regulation and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/ATF surveillance and international electronic funds transfer reporting. Canada does not maintain a separate foreign-exchange control ministry; exchange-control functions are absorbed into the federal banking and payments architecture.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada adheres to IMF Article VIII obligations and maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. The Canadian dollar is freely floating; there are no general exchange-control restrictions, no central-bank permission for inward capital calls, and no blanket profit-remittance licensing. Regulatory hurdles are confined to anti-money-laundering reporting, sanctions screening, and tax compliance. Cross-border dividends, interest, and management fees paid by a Quebec corporation may be subject to non-resident withholding tax under the Income Tax Act (Part XIII) and, where applicable, reduced by the Canada-Quebec treaty network or the Canada-U.S. treaty in the case of U.S. investors. Capital repatriation and loan repayments are unrestricted aside from treaty and anti-avoidance provisions such as thin capitalization and general anti-avoidance rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no timeline for repatriation of export proceeds or foreign receipts. Exporters and fund managers may hold foreign currency in domestic or offshore accounts. Nevertheless, all international electronic fund transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported by the financial intermediary to FINTRAC; the entity should maintain underlying export, investment, or capital-call documentation to demonstrate the commercial or investment purpose of each forex flow.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low. Offshore digital EMI (electronic money institution) accounts cannot serve as primary capital-call or escrow rails for a Quebec venture-capital general partner because they are not authorized Canadian deposit-taking institutions and do not benefit from Canadian deposit insurance or OSFI prudential oversight. Such platforms may be used for non-core disbursement support only if they are registered with FINTRAC as a money services business (MSB) and meet Quebec's virtual-currency and payment-provider licensing expectations. The principal legal constraints are the requirement for a Canadian domestic bank account for subscription escrow, the prohibition on accepting unlicensed deposit business, FINTRAC registration, sanctions compliance, and the inability of an offshore EMI to issue a Canadian clearing-routing number (CAD) or provide a SWIFT correspondent relationship that satisfies institutional limited-partner expectations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no absolute statutory requirement that directors appear physically at a Quebec branch, but in practice all major Schedule I banks require at least one mandated signatory, usually a director or senior officer, to complete an identity verification interview. Remote opening is increasingly possible through bank-approved video KYC where the entity is already a client, where the signatory holds a valid government-issued Canadian ID, and where the director's identity can be corroborated against the provincial business registry. Where no Canadian resident director exists, the bank may require physical appearance at a Canadian branch, notarized certified true copies, apostilled corporate documents, and an in-person or notarized verification of the non-resident director. Quebec civil-law practice may also require a notarial attestation for certain corporate resolutions and mandate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Venture capital general partner with non-resident limited partners and no prior Canadian banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified certificate of incorporation or continuance, Quebec register extract (Registraire des entreprises), full constitutional documents, partnership agreement, limited-partner subscription agreements, fund term sheet, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth letters, investor beneficial-ownership waterfall, audited or reviewed financial statements, org chart identifying all directors and ultimate beneficial owners, sanctions/PEP rationalization, and legal opinion from Quebec counsel confirming the GP's authority to open accounts and receive capital calls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital calls and subscription wires from foreign-currency jurisdictions routed through correspondent banks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital-call notices matched to LP commitments, bank statements showing upstream source account in the investor's name, SWIFT MT103 with clear payment purpose narrative, investor-side AML/KYC packs, investor-country tax identification/CRS/FATCA self-certifications, and the fund's closing statement or notarized closing index identifying each subscription.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments, management fee rebates, carried-interest distributions, or payments from pooled fund accounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed partnership agreement and GP compensation schedule, Limited Partnership Act-compliant capital account statements, fund administrator's NAV report, distribution waterfall model, board resolutions approving each disbursement, and copy of the GP's written AML policy for third-party payment screening and travel-rule compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure or non-resident ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence file including biographical information, independent source-of-wealth report, corporate registry and corporate-listing search results, tax residence certificates, criminal-record/sanctions screening, transaction rationale, economic-substance documentation, and a written approval from the bank's Compliance Officer for high-risk client acceptance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory licensing and regulatory registration as a Quebec exempt-market dealer or portfolio manager
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current certificate of registration issued by the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF), NI 31-103 registration or exemption documentation, notice of exempt market dealer registration, chief compliance officer attestation, Form 33-109F6 records, and confirmation that the GP is permitted to solicit accredited investors under applicable securities legislation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital calls should be routed via SWIFT MT103 through the Quebec GP's domestic Canadian clearing account held with a Schedule I bank. Payment instructions must identify the Canadian beneficiary GP, the fund's capital-call account, and the LP investor's name and account. Although Canada does not maintain a centralized payment-purpose coding system, each MT103 narrative must state the commercial purpose clearly, e.g., 'Capital contribution to [Fund] per call notice dated [date]'. The Canadian receiving bank will perform sanctions and FINTRAC reporting for wires of CAD 10,000 or greater; the GP should pre-submit the capital-call notice, subscription agreement excerpt, and beneficial-ownership data to the relationship manager before the first wire to avoid extended KYC holds. Multi-currency inbound flows may be converted into CAD or held in USD sub-accounts; conversion is unrestricted but should be documented at the then-prevailing market rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for investment disbursements and fund expenses should be executed either through SWIFT MT103 for direct cash transfers or through commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) where a financing structure requires a bank guarantee. For VC-stage investments, standard outbound rails include: (i) domestic wire via the Canadian Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for CAD payments; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for cross-border USD/EUR/CAD wires; and (iii) Secure Payment of trade-related milestones using a commercial LC only when the underlying investment agreement contains documentary delivery conditions. All outbound wires require the GP's executed disbursement resolution, amended capital call, or investment committee approval, and must pass FINTRAC's $10,000 international EFT reporting threshold, the receiving bank's AML screening, and Quebec's securities and privacy-law constraints on disclosing LP information to the receiving bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards (forwards traded with OSFI-regulated Canadian chartered banks)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic or restricted currencies, executed with an authorized bank or prime broker
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps) for matching capital-call currency and investment-currency exposure
Plain-vanilla FX options (call/put options) used to hedge committed capital inflows and future transaction settlements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following each anniversary of the enterprise's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 200–1,000; two consecutive missed annual declarations trigger administrative dissolution of the enterprise.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the sixth month after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month late (maximum 12 months); daily compound interest on overdue amounts; prolonged non-compliance may lead to criminal prosecution and director liability assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of the sixth month after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (up to 12%); interest charged on deficiencies; repeated non-filing may lead to prosecution and suspension of permits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit is required for a private venture capital GP corporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act unless any shareholder requests one or the corporation is a reporting issuer. An audit may be waived annually by unanimous shareholder resolution. If waived, a review engagement may be required under the terms of investment fund limited partnership agreements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable reporting issuers; private enterprises may elect Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) or IFRS on a consistent basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec's Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises requires the annual declaration to confirm and update ultimate beneficial ownership information. Any transfer of shares resulting in an individual holding 25% or more of voting shares or control must be disclosed to the registrar within 15 days of the change. The company must also maintain a current UBO register and make it available to the registrar upon request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Minutes of directors' and shareholders' meetings)
